structured_output.what_is_happening: "Binance Accelerationism" (b/acc) was deployed directly as a PumpSwap pool about 11 minutes before detection. It did not migrate from the pump.fun bonding curve (migrated_unix=0). The price is up about 700% and the market cap is about $96k. The token description is only a BSC-style contract address (0xcf57…7777), and the GeckoTerminal X handle is @binance. That makes this look like a Solana copy of a BNB-chain "b/acc" meme. Another Solana token with the same name was created about 3 minutes earlier and already has near-zero liquidity. The biggest problem is ownership: one non-AMM wallet holds 80.57% of supply, and 100% of the LP is unlocked. Buyers and sellers are badly unbalanced: 2,047 unique buyers against 36 unique sellers. GMGN tags 83% of traders as bot/degen, which points to buys spread across many bot wallets rather than organic demand.

authenticity.evidence: 2,047 unique buyers vs 36 sellers within minutes. Bot/degen rate is 0.83 and GMGN tags 10 wallets as bundlers. One wallet holds 80.57% of supply. The pool was deployed directly with no curve phase. No socials.
authenticity.uncertainty: The 80.57% holder could be a locker or burn account that RugCheck did not label. I could not verify this.

structural_risks: A single wallet holds 80.57% of supply, a huge overhang against about $30k of liquidity
100% of LP unlocked; the creator can pull liquidity
Launched directly on PumpSwap, not via the pump.fun curve
A same-name token launched minutes earlier already has about $0 liquidity, which suggests a serial rug pattern

structured_output.counterargument: Buy pressure is heavy (about 9:1 buys to sells) and turnover is about 5.7x per hour. If the 80% holder is actually a lock or burn that RugCheck did not label, this bot-driven momentum could push a $96k coin to $200k within minutes, and a 2x is easy at this size.
